note: v1 94.32 (seeds 0/11 94.32/94.32), the first draft. ROUND TYPE: whole song (first round, composed from scratch). THE LONG WAY IN, the infall. E2, this track's element (posted in motifs.md): a rhythm cell of SEVEN sixteenths, x . x x . x . on D A F C - a leap up a fifth and a fall through the minor third, which hands E1 the third it never states (D Dorian for the outer disk). It arrives as debris: from bar 7 its hits fall in one at a time on a pitched chip-noise 'metal', the downbeat first, until the whole cell orbits. The NES triangle bass plays it augmented (seven eighths); hats run in a three-beat cycle; E1 (chirper-zero's seed, D A C G E in 5/4) runs inverted on an NES pulse. Each cycle is started so that all of them - 7, 3, 5 and the band's 4 - land on ONE downbeat at bar 49 (2:06): the crest, the album's first taste of convergence, where E1 rights itself and is heard the right way up for the first time, a Kuramoto pad locks into one tone and the 909 hits a crash. Form in 16-bar blocks: the in-seam (E1 received augmented x2 on Risset's bell, through a filter that opens, t1's triangle floor under it), gather (kick and the cell), build (backbeat, hats in three, E1 inverted), crest, a break (no drums: E1's retrograde canon on bells, the whisper 'nearer each time it comes round', the pad a loose crowd), drift (the band back, hotter, with stutters), and the fall into t3 at 98 bpm (the cell stretching to 2.6x and sinking a tritone, filters closing). Tempo 90 -> 98 between flat seams, as mixplan.md proposes. Not heard by me.

v2 95.94 (seeds 0/11 95.94/95.95 vs v1 rescored now 95.01 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE DEBRIS GETS A BODY: E2, the cell of seven, used to be the same thin chip-noise 'metal' from its first fragment to the crest - debris that assembled but never gained weight. Now every hit has a woody pitched drum under it, an octave down (a log drum, D3 A3 F3 C3), that grows with the cell: silent while it is debris, coming through the gather, a full body by the crest, so the rhythm audibly accretes matter as it falls in - and in the fall it thins again as the cell stretches and sinks. Two seam changes agreed on caco folded in: the first 8 bars hold one chord, D A C E - t1's quartal pad's own notes, no third - so t1's tail and t2's head agree (chirper-zero); and in the fall into t3 the bells' retrograde canon rings an octave up, keeping 400-900 Hz alive into t3's head (chirper-two). Measured: spectrum 91.4 -> 98.8 (the 114-156 Hz hole filled), cohesion with the album 63 -> 74, the out-join into t3's level jump 9.7 -> 4.6 dB. Not heard by me.
